_comment: Source of truth for every asset. `tools/task.py next` reads this and hands you one job. Sizes are VOXELS (8 vox = 1 m). See docs/SCALE.md.

batches.lab: Phase 1 — the scale lab. Everything needed to answer 'does this scale read?' Nothing here is final art; it is production-quality blockout that we keep if it reads.
batches.kit: Phase 2 — the minimum modular kit. Not started until the lab passes.
batches.slice: Phase 3 — one house, one yard, one street segment, made to actually play.

assets.name: ground_grass_1x1m
assets.title: Grass ground tile
assets.brief: The single most repeated object in the game. A 1 m square of lawn, 0.25 m thick so it can sit proud of a road surface. Top face is the only face that will ever be seen; the sides matter only where the tile meets a road or a creek bank.
must: Fills the full 20 x 20 x 5 box with no gaps — tiles must butt seamlessly on all four sides
Top surface uses at least two greens so a field of these is not a flat colour, but no single-voxel speckle noise
Any variation must tile with ITSELF rotated 90/180/270 without an obvious seam

assets.name: char_civilian_base
assets.title: Base civilian character
assets.brief: The body every character in the game is built from. Neutral clothing, neutral pose, standing straight, arms at sides, facing -Y (toward the camera). This is not a character, it is the mannequin. Roles get added later as colour and accessories on top of this exact silhouette.
must: Exactly 14 voxels tall (1.75 m) — this is the number the entire game is calibrated to
Head roughly 8 x 8 x 8 at the top
Shoulders 5 wide, body 3 deep — 4 makes the legs read as slabs
Readable as a person at 23 screen pixels tall — test by squinting
Face detail is a waste at this size; a suggestion of eyes at most
Feet centred on the model's X/Y centre so the pivot lands between them

assets.name: wall_exterior_doorway_2m
assets.title: Exterior wall with doorway (2 m)
assets.brief: A 2 m run of exterior house wall with a standard doorway punched through it. This is 2 m wide, not 1 m, because a 1 m module with a 1 m opening would be nothing but a hole. Includes the door frame; the door leaf itself is a separate asset.
must: Opening is exactly 20 wide x 40 tall (1 x 2 m), centred in X, sitting on the floor (z = 0)
Wall is exactly 5 voxels thick and exactly 55 tall
Left and right edges are flat and full-height so it butts against wall_exterior_straight_1m seamlessly
Frame reads clearly from the game camera — this is how the player finds entrances
Interior face and exterior face may differ in colour

assets.name: wall_exterior_straight_1m
assets.title: Exterior wall, straight (1 m)
assets.brief: The plain 1 m run of exterior wall. The most-repeated structural piece. Boring on purpose — all the personality comes from colour variants and from the window and doorway modules breaking it up.
must: Fills 20 x 5 x 55 exactly, with flat left/right/top edges so runs tile seamlessly
Siding or texture pattern must repeat cleanly every 20 voxels
Do not model a baseboard or trim into this piece — it must work as both a ground-floor and upper-floor wall

assets.name: floor_wood_1x1m
assets.title: Wood floor tile
assets.brief: Interior floorboards, 1 m square, 0.25 m slab. Seen constantly through cutaway roofs, so it sets the interior mood more than any prop does.
must: Fills 20 x 20 x 5 exactly and tiles seamlessly on all four sides
Board direction runs along +X so a room reads as having a floor grain direction
Must still read as floor when 80 percent covered by furniture

assets.name: wall_interior_straight_1m
assets.title: Interior wall, straight (1 m)
assets.brief: Room divider. Half the thickness of an exterior wall so interiors do not eat floor space. Seen mostly as a thin line from above plus one visible face.
must: Exactly 1 voxel thick — this is the thinnest thing in the game and it must still read
Both faces may be different colours (different rooms)
Flat left/right/top edges for seamless tiling

assets.name: door_exterior
assets.title: Exterior door leaf
assets.brief: The swinging leaf that fills a standard doorway. Modelled closed, in its own file, so the game can rotate it around its hinge edge. The hinge is the -X edge.
must: Exactly 8 x 1 x 16 — must exactly fill the doorway opening
Hinge edge is the -X (left) edge; the handle is on the +X edge
Handle is readable from the game camera even though it is 1 voxel

assets.name: chair_dining
assets.title: Dining chair
assets.brief: The smallest piece of real furniture in the game, and therefore the hardest legibility test. If a chair does not read at this scale, the scale is wrong.
must: Seat surface at exactly 10 voxels (0.5 m) high
Back rises to 18 voxels total
Legs may be 2 voxels but the seat and back must be at least 4 voxels thick
Faces -Y (a person sitting in it looks toward the camera)

assets.name: table_dining_small
assets.title: Dining table
assets.brief: A four-seat dining table, 1 x 1.5 m. Pairs with chair_dining — the two together are the main readability test for interiors.
must: Top surface at exactly 15 voxels (0.75 m) high
Top is at least 4 voxels thick
Four chairs must be able to tuck under it without intersecting the legs

assets.name: bed_single
assets.title: Single bed
assets.brief: 1 x 2 m bed. Beds are the anchor object that tells the player 'this is a bedroom' in one glance from directly above, so the top-down silhouette matters far more than the sides.
must: Mattress top at 13 voxels (0.65 m)
Pillow at the +Y end, clearly readable from directly above
Blanket colour must contrast with floor_wood_1x1m

assets.name: sofa_two_seat
assets.title: Two-seat sofa
assets.brief: 2 m sofa. The living-room anchor, and a likely cover object, so its silhouette needs to read as something you could crouch behind.
must: Seat surface at 10 voxels, back and arms to 18
Faces -Y
Back is at least 4 voxels thick so it reads as solid cover

assets.name: kitchen_counter_1m
assets.title: Kitchen counter (1 m)
assets.brief: A 1 m run of kitchen counter with cabinet below and worktop above. Tiles in runs along +X, so treat it as architecture rather than as a prop.
must: Exactly 20 wide so runs tile seamlessly — flat, full left and right edges
Worktop at exactly 18 voxels (0.9 m), at least 2 voxels thick, in a contrasting colour to the cabinet
Cabinet front faces -Y
Toe-kick recess at the bottom front is worth the 3 voxels it costs

assets.name: wall_exterior_window_2m
assets.title: Exterior wall with window (2 m)
assets.brief: 2 m exterior wall run with a window punched through. Windows are a primary stealth affordance — the player will look for them as climb-in routes — so the opening must be obvious at a glance.
must: Opening exactly 20 wide x 25 tall, centred in X, sill top at z = 18 (0.9 m)
Glass filled with the glass colour, 2 voxels thick, set into the middle of the wall
Frame reads clearly from the game camera
Left/right/top edges flat and full so it tiles with the straight wall

assets.name: stairs_straight_full
assets.title: Straight staircase (full storey)
assets.brief: A full-storey straight run: 11 steps of 0.25 m rise and 0.3125 m run, climbing 2.75 m over 3.5 m of depth. Stairs are the trickiest thing to read from a near-overhead camera, so this asset is a genuine test of the camera angle.
must: Exactly 11 steps, each 5 voxels rise and 6 voxels run
Bottom step starts at z = 0 at the -Y end; top step surface lands at exactly z = 55
1 m wide (20 voxels)
Step nosings need enough colour contrast to count the steps from above

assets.name: ground_asphalt_1x1m
assets.title: Asphalt road tile
assets.brief: Road surface, 1 m square. Road markings are decals added later, not modelled into this tile.
must: Fills 20 x 20 x 5 exactly, tiles seamlessly and rotation-invariantly
Noticeably darker than sidewalk and grass so the road reads as a distinct region from above
No markings, no cracks that would repeat visibly across a 6 m road

assets.name: sidewalk_straight_1m
assets.title: Sidewalk section (1 m run)
assets.brief: 1 m of sidewalk, full 1.5 m depth. Runs along +X. Sidewalks are the main NPC pathing spine of the level, so they need to read as a walkable channel from directly above.
must: Exactly 20 (run) x 30 (depth) x 5
A slab joint line every 1 m along the run, so a long sidewalk shows rhythm
Clearly lighter than asphalt and clearly distinct from grass

assets.name: curb_straight_1m
assets.title: Curb (1 m)
assets.brief: The 0.25 m lip between sidewalk and road. Tiny, but it is what makes the street cross-section read as a real street instead of two flat colours.
must: Exactly 20 x 5 x 5
Top face and road-facing face in different values so the lip catches the eye from above

assets.name: fence_wood_straight_1m
assets.title: Wood fence (1 m)
assets.brief: 1 m of picket fence, 1.25 m tall — chest height on a 1.75 m character, i.e. climbable. Fences define lot boundaries and therefore define most of the level's routing.
must: Exactly 20 wide with flat left/right edges so runs tile
10 tall (1.25 m) — must read as climbable, not as a wall
Gaps between pickets must be visible from the game camera, because you can see through a fence and that matters for stealth
Posts at the tile edges so a run does not show doubled posts

assets.name: hedge_straight_1m
assets.title: Hedge (1 m)
assets.brief: 1 m of trimmed hedge, 1 m deep and 1.25 m tall. The opaque counterpart to the fence: same height, but you cannot see through it. That contrast is a gameplay rule expressed purely in art.
must: Exactly 20 wide with flat left/right edges for tiling
Visually solid — no see-through gaps, this is the whole point versus the fence
Silhouette must be slightly irregular on top so a long run does not read as an extruded rectangle
Irregularity must still tile with itself

assets.name: bush_large
assets.title: Large bush (hiding spot)
assets.brief: A 1.5 m round bush big enough for a character to hide inside. This is a gameplay object dressed as scenery, so it must be visually distinguishable from decorative shrubs — the player has to learn 'that shape means I can hide there'.
must: At least 30 x 30 footprint and 25 tall so a 36-voxel character crouching is plausibly concealed
Rounded silhouette, distinct from the flat-topped hedge
Lighter or more saturated than hedge_straight_1m so it reads as a different class of object

assets.name: tree_deciduous_small
assets.title: Small deciduous tree
assets.brief: A 3 x 3 m, 4 m tall tree. Trees will be faded or cut away when they cover the player, so build the canopy as one or two solid masses — never as individual leaves.
must: Trunk and canopy as separate simple masses; no per-leaf modelling
Canopy silhouette irregular enough to not read as a sphere
Trunk centred on the footprint so the pivot lands in it
Must look acceptable when the canopy is faded to 40 percent opacity

assets.name: mailbox
assets.title: Mailbox
assets.brief: Roadside mailbox on a post, 1 m tall. The smallest prop in the lab, included specifically to find the floor of what is worth modelling at this scale.
must: Exactly 20 tall (1 m)
Box reads as a box from above, not as a blob
If this does not read, say so — that is a useful result, not a failure

assets.name: car_sedan
assets.title: Sedan
assets.brief: 1.75 x 4 x 1.5 m family car. Cars are the largest props in the level and set the upper bound on prop legibility. Recolours will provide all the variety, so keep the body shape neutral.
must: Exactly 80 long (4 m) and no more than 30 tall (1.5 m)
Windows in the glass colour so it reads as a car and not a loaf, from directly above
Faces +Y (front of car toward +Y)
Body colour confined to a small number of voxels' worth of distinct regions so recolouring is trivial

assets.name: wall_exterior_broken_a
assets.title: Exterior wall, broken (variant A)
assets.brief: The blown-out version of wall_exterior_straight_1m, built now rather than months later. Swapping straight-to-broken is the entire Tier 2/3 destruction mechanic, and the swap only sells if the two pieces share exact footprint and colour.
must: Same 20 x 5 footprint and same colours as wall_exterior_straight_1m
Roughly the lower third survives; the break edge is jagged and irregular
Break must not extend past the 8 x 2 footprint — no debris modelled in, debris is separate
Exposed interior structure (studs, brick core) in a contrasting colour sells the damage more than the jagged edge does
